name: MIC2026-1YM-TR
title: MIC2026 / MIC2076: two-channel high-side power distribution switch, 2.7 V to 5.5 V, 500 mA per channel
summary: Two independent MOSFET high-side switches in one 8-lead SOIC, each with its own enable input and its own open-drain fault output. Each channel conducts 500 mA or more continuously with 140 mΩ maximum on-resistance at 5 V, limits its current, and has its own thermal sensor; a second, higher die-temperature trip turns off both channels. The switch blocks current from output to input when off, soft-starts its output to hold down inrush into capacitive loads, delays the fault flag by about 3 ms so short inrush events do not report, and stays off below its undervoltage threshold. The MIC2026 restarts by itself after a thermal trip; the MIC2076 latches the faulted output off until the load is taken away or the enable input is cycled. The -1 suffix has active-high enables, the -2 suffix active-low.
key_figures: 90 mΩ typ, 140 mΩ max at VIN = 5V, IOUT = 500 mA
0.5 A min, 0.9 A typ, 1.25 A max

notes: The code reads device, then enable (-1 active-high, -2 active-low), then Y for –40°C to +85°C, then M for the 8-lead SOIC, then -TR for tape and reel; no suffix means tubes.
MIC2026 and MIC2076 differ in what follows a thermal trip: the MIC2026 turns its output back on as the die cools, the MIC2076 holds the output off until the load is removed or the enable is toggled.
The -TR suffix is an ordering code only and does not appear on the part.

Top marking is three lines: product code (2026), then the suffix (-1YM, or -2YM for the -2 versions), then a week code and traceability code. The SOIC is lead-free; the matte-tin JEDEC e3 mark sits on the outer packing.

pins.name: ENA
pins.function: Enable for switch A, logic level. High turns the switch on in the -1 versions; low turns it on in the -2 versions.

pins.name: FLGA
pins.function: Fault flag for channel A, pulled low on overcurrent or thermal shutdown. The flag goes low on overcurrent only when it persists beyond tD.

pins.name: FLGB
pins.function: Fault flag for channel B, pulled low on overcurrent or thermal shutdown. The flag goes low on overcurrent only when it persists beyond tD.

pins.name: ENB
pins.function: Enable for switch B, logic level. High turns the switch on in the -1 versions; low turns it on in the -2 versions.

pins.name: IN
pins.function: Supply for the control logic and the drain of both output switches.

circuits.title: Typical application, MIC2026-2 under a logic controller
circuits.description: An MIC2026-2 switches a 2.7 V to 5.5 V supply to two loads. IN has 0.1 µF to ground. A logic controller, powered from the control rail VCONT, drives ENA and ENB with active-low on/off lines and reads FLGA and FLGB on its two overcurrent inputs; each flag is pulled up to VCONT through 10 kΩ. Each output feeds a load returned to ground.

circuits.title: Hot-plug USB peripheral
circuits.description: A USB peripheral that plugs into a live port. Cable VBUS has 4.7 µF to ground, feeds the USB controller and the switch IN, and a capacitor runs from IN to GND. ENA and ENB are tied to ground and the flags are left open. Each output drives one USB function block with its own bulk capacitor CBULK to ground. The switch soft-starts both outputs so the bulk capacitance does not pull a large inrush from the port.
notes: U1 is the MIC2076, marked SPN010012.
Only the USB controller supply connection belongs to this circuit.

circuits.title: RC filter on the fault flag
circuits.description: FLGA is pulled up to V+ through 10 kΩ and reaches the controller's overcurrent input through a series R with C to ground at the controller side. The RC delays the flag so a long inrush transient, longer than the internal tD filter, does not reach the controller. The other switch pins are not connected in this circuit.

circuits.title: USB two-port host
circuits.description: A self-powered host with two downstream ports. A 5.0 V rail feeds IN with 0.1 µF to GND. Upstream VBUS (4.50 V to 5.25 V, 100 mA max) feeds an MIC5207-3.3 regulator with 1 µF on its input and 1 µF on its 3.3 V output; that rail powers the 3.3 V USB controller and pulls FLGA and FLGB up through 10 kΩ each. The controller drives ENA and ENB and reads both flags. Each output feeds a port's VBUS through a ferrite bead, with 47 µF (polarised) from the output to ground; each port's ground also runs through a ferrite bead. Upstream and downstream data lines go to the controller.

parts.value: Upstream USB, VBUS 4.50 V to 5.25 V, 100 mA max

circuits.title: USB two-port bus-powered hub
circuits.description: A hub powered from its upstream port. Upstream VBUS (4.50 V to 5.25 V) feeds the switch IN directly, with 0.1 µF to GND, and also an MIC5207-3.3 regulator with 1 µF at its input and 1 µF at its 3.3 V output. The 3.3 V rail powers the USB controller, pulls FLGA and FLGB up through 10 kΩ each, and pulls upstream D+ up through 1.5 kΩ 2%. The controller drives ENA and ENB and reads both flags, so it can switch each downstream port. The outputs reach the two downstream ports through ferrite beads with 47 µF (polarised) at each output; port grounds also pass through ferrite beads.

operation.text: IN supplies the logic and is the drain of each output MOSFET; each OUT is a source. Load current normally runs IN to OUT. While a channel is on, the switch conducts both ways, so if VOUT rises above VIN current runs back from OUT to IN. While a channel is off, the output may be held above IN without current flowing back into IN: there is no body diode path.

Each channel has its own temperature sensor. A channel that is in current limit turns off and pulls its flag low when the die reaches 140 °C; the other channel keeps running. Above 160 °C both channels turn off. The MIC2026 turns the output back on when the die cools to 120 °C, and keeps cycling on and off with the flag following until the fault clears or the channel is disabled. The MIC2076 latches the output off and sources a small pull-up current into the output, so the latch clears by itself when the load (for example a USB device) is unplugged; cycling EN also clears it. Depending on board layout, package and ambient, the trip can take several hundred milliseconds after the fault starts; a hard short on the output trips fastest.

The limit is fixed inside the part and allows at least 500 mA to the load. Current is measured on a sampled fraction of the switch current, so there is no sense resistor drop. Enabled into a short or heavy load, the channel goes straight into constant-current mode with the output voltage pulled down, and the flag reports the overcurrent. If a short lands on a channel that is already on, a large current can flow briefly before the limit responds, after which current is held below the short-circuit limit. With a slowly rising load, the channel supplies the load until the current-limit threshold is reached, then changes to constant current, with a foldback of about 200 mA.

Each FLG is an open-drain NMOS output, pulled low on overcurrent or thermal shutdown. An overcurrent is reported only after the flag delay tD (3 ms typ), so short inrush when a capacitive load is hot-plugged, which can exceed the limit for up to 1 ms, does not set the flag.
The output switch stays off until VIN rises past about 2.5 V. The lockout is active only while the channel is enabled.
Put 0.1 µF to 1 µF from IN to GND close to the part. Without it, a short on the output can ring the input through the supply lead inductance hard enough to damage the internal control circuits.

The integrated charge pumps turn each switch on slowly, so an enabled switch moves from high to low impedance gradually and limits inrush into capacitive loads, which suits hot-plug boards. With very large load capacitance (more than 400 µF) the inrush can last longer than the flag delay and the flag goes low during it. An external RC on the flag line hides this: choose its time constant as the transient duration minus tD(MIN).

A USB host port must deliver at least 500 mA at 5 V ±5%, keep the delivered power under 25 VA, and report overcurrent to the host. A hub needs at least 120 µF of bulk capacitance for hot-plug, preferably low-ESR electrolytic or tantalum. A bus-powered hub must switch each downstream port under host control and may have up to four ports of 100 mA at 4.4 V minimum; it may draw 500 mA from upstream but only 100 mA until it has enumerated, so soft start is needed to limit droop on upstream VBUS. Bus-powered peripherals without downstream ports have the same requirements.
The two channels are thermally isolated, and the parts are pin-compatible with the MIC2526. UL file E179633.
